To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a microchip to analyze synovial fluid, a sample that is difficult to analyze, and that we were able to capture cells from the sample using a chip.
a microfluidic device was developed for the first time to capture and analyze specific WBC subpoputions from synovial aspirate samples in miniscule amounts of sample volume.
we have designed a novel microfluidic platform to achieve repeatable standardized synovial analysis from miniscule volume of synovia fluid aspirate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a microfluidic device to isolate and analyze white blood cells from a small volume (100 μl) of patient synovials fluid.
developing a novel platform to isolate WBC subpopulation from patient synovial samples for standardized point-of-care analysis of joint health and disease.
the development of an integrated microfluidic platform for the first time for the isolation of WBCs from synovial aspirate and the analysis of WBCs based on their specific surface markers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we developed a microchip-based method for the first time for simultaneous isolation and analysis of specific cell surface marker-expressing cells (CD4+, CD8+ and CD66b+) in the joint from miniscule synovial fluid volumes.
the microfluidic platform is capable of isolating WBC subpopulation from miniscule volume of synovia fluid samples.
the Synovial chip allows the isolation of WBC sub-populations from small volume of synovium fluid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Synovial Chip is the first microfluidic device that can capture WBC subpopulation cells from synovial aspirate samples.
we have developed a microfluidics-based platform for the analysis of synovia fluid samples.
we have developed a microfluidics-based platform for standardized and automated synovial fluid analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microfluidic technology can provide a platform for rapid, standardized, and cost-effective analysis of synovitis and other joint pathologies in the clinic.
Synovial Chip provides a platform for standardized and automated synovial fluid analysis in the clinic.

the Synovial Chip provides an opportunity for standardized synovial cell analysis in the clinic, with potential applications for the diagnosis and monitoring of inflammatory and infectious joint diseases.
